articles.title: America’s not actually polarized. It can agree on Mr. Beast — and Joe Rogan
articles.summary: A study of 741 people found that Americans often agree on popular culture figures like Mr. Beast and Joe Rogan. The research suggests that entertainment, including influencers and podcasts, serves as an important source of political information that is frequently omitted from other studies. Because politics are intertwined with popular culture, these shared preferences indicate that the United States may not be as polarized as commonly believed.
articles.description: We asked 741 people to name their top influencers, podcasts, comedians, musicians, video games, films and TV series and found the United States of America.
